Two commemorative collections have approved exceptions: **Little Frights** and **Troves After Dark** explorers each contribute **150 stamina**, even though their edition size would normally fall in the 75-stamina band.

### How to Bank Troves and Build Progress

**Banking is the primary way to increase your Upland Progression level at launch.** Banking means permanently depositing Troves into the **Trove Vault** to meet progression requirements and work toward rewards.

- **Open your Trove Wallet** and choose a Trove you have collected.
- **Review its available banking tier.** Bronze and Silver are available in this first release, and the required quantity can vary by Trove.
- **Use the bank action when you hold enough copies.** The banking option becomes available when your inventory meets the requirement.
- **Confirm the permanent deposit.** Banked Troves cannot be withdrawn, returned to spendable inventory, or used in recipes later. That final step matters. A Trove in your inventory remains available for future recipes and other uses as those systems arrive. A Trove placed in the Vault becomes part of your permanent banking achievement instead.

*Banking interface preview*

Each Trove has its own banked tier, while your profile has an **overall Upland Progression level**. Banking Troves helps move that overall level forward. Your profile shows the next milestone and its available reward, giving you a clear goal without requiring you to memorize the whole progression path.

*Your profile shows your Upland Progression level and the next milestone.*

The** beta** begins strictly with Troves as the progression requirement. **Additional types of requirements** may be introduced later after the team has **real usage data**. The opening levels are designed to teach the collection and banking loop, so their pace and rewards **should not be treated as the final depth of progression**.

### Crafting: What Comes Next

Crafting is an important part of the larger Troves system, but **it is not available on launch day**. Here is how the loop will work as recipes roll out:

- **Discover a Trove.** The first discovery reveals recipes that consume that Trove.
- **Collect the ingredients.** A recipe becomes ready when you hold its required Troves.
- **Go to the Service Structure where the recipe is available.** Recipes are accessed on the Service Structure itself, not from a generic property menu.
- **Fulfill the recipe.** Crafting consumes the listed ingredients and grants the recipe’s stated result. Recipes can also provide additional bonus rewards.
- **Explore deeper combinations.** Some crafted Troves can become ingredients in later recipes, creating higher-level paths over time. Players select a recipe, not its bonus roll. The stated result provides the recipe’s default outcome, while any additional rewards can vary. This lets crafting have surprises without turning the basic result into a completely unknown outcome.

### What the Phased Beta Builds Toward

### What the Phased Beta Builds Toward

The launch set of 189 collectible Troves is **the first batch**, not the full catalog. Across the rollout, the team is preparing **over 500 Troves and a much deeper recipe system**. New Troves, recipes, and banking tiers will arrive in regular batches over the coming weeks, **allowing the system to grow** without asking players to understand every layer at once.

The beta also gives the team room to **tune collection activity**, **reward pacing**, **progression requirements**, and** overall balance**. Early mechanics and rewards can change as real play reveals what is working and what needs adjustment. Later systems, including broader plant interactions, automation, and farming, are part of the future direction rather than today’s first release.

For now, the best way to begin is simple: move your Block Explorer, try different Service Structures and plants, fill your wallet, compare discoveries with other players, and **choose carefully **before banking anything permanently.

### Start Exploring Today

What will your first Trove be? Which discoveries will you preserve in your Vault, and which will you hold for the recipes still to come?

Troves are going live today. [Bring back a friend](https://playupland.com/Medium1) who has been waiting for a fresh reason to explore, invite someone new to discover their first neighborhood, and share what you find. This next part of Upland will be more fun when the community uncovers it together.

# Troves Launch Weekend: Collect, Bank, and Compete

October 22, 2026

***Editor’s note**: Trove Bankers leaderboard scoring has been updated to recognize higher banking tiers. Each eligible Trove type earns 1 point at Bronze or 3 points at Silver, with only its highest tier counting. Upgrading from Bronze to Silver adds 2 points to your score. Trove Collectors scoring and all announced prizes remain unchanged.*

*
*

Troves are **now live** in Upland, and we’re celebrating with a first-weekend challenge:** collect Troves, bank Troves, and compete for up to 1.75 million UPX in prizes**. From launch through **Monday, October 26 at 9:00 a.m. PT**, explore structures and plants, build your collection, and make your first permanent deposits. Bring a returning friend or a first-time player, compare finds, and make the first Troves weekend one to remember.

Then, **join the Upland team next Tuesday **for Troves: The Bigger Picture, a live conversation with Upland Co-Founder Idan Zuckerman about** why Troves are a major step for Upland**, what we’re learning from the launch, and **what’s coming next**. Get hands-on this weekend, then join us to explore where Troves will take Upland.

[See the live stream here](https://www.youtube.com/live/FVsi4UQPNTo).

### Two Ways to Compete

There is no entry form or screenshot submission. Eligible game activity during the competition window counts automatically.

- **Trove Collectors:** Ranked by the total number of individual Troves collected from structures and plants during the competition. Every eligible Trove, including duplicates, counts as one. Trove Dust, opening inventory, promotional or administrative grants, quiz rewards, and purchased packs do not count. Banking never reduces your Collector score: it measures earned collection quantity, not what remains in your inventory.
- **Trove Bankers:** Trove Bankers: Climb the leaderboard by banking different Troves and upgrading them to Silver. Each Bronze-banked Trove type earns 1 point, while each Silver-banked Trove type earns 3 points. Only your highest tier for each Trove type counts, so upgrading from Bronze to Silver adds 2 points to your score You can compete on **both leaderboards**, earn ranked prizes on both, and collect both leaderboard badges if you finish in the top 25 on each.

### Prizes for Each Leaderboard

The following UPX ladder applies **separately to Trove Collectors and Trove Bankers**:

- **1st:** 100,000 UPX
- **2nd:** 75,000 UPX
- **3rd:** 50,000 UPX
- **4th–10th:** 25,000 UPX each
- **11th–25th:** 15,000 UPX each Every top-25 finisher also earns that leaderboard’s badge. All top-25 Collectors receive the same **Troves Launch Weekend: Collector****badge**, and all top-25 Bankers receive the same **Troves Launch Weekend: Banker****badge**. There is one badge for each leaderboard, not a different badge for each placement.

### Participation Draw

You do not need a top-25 finish to have a chance at UPX. Up to **50 qualifying players** who do not receive a ranked top-25 prize on either leaderboard will be selected at random, without replacement, to receive **10,000 UPX each**.

### Participation Draw

You do not need a top-25 finish to have a chance at UPX. Up to **50 qualifying players** who do not receive a ranked top-25 prize on either leaderboard will be selected at random, without replacement, to receive **10,000 UPX each**.

To earn one entry in the participation draw, complete both requirements during the competition:

- Collect at least **10 eligible non-Dust Troves on each of two different PT calendar dates**. Collection quantities count, not ten separate collection attempts, and the same source exclusions used for the Trove Collectors leaderboard apply.
- Bank enough eligible Troves to reach **Bronze on at least three distinct eligible Trove types** during the event. Each qualifying player receives **one entry**, no matter how far beyond the requirements they go. Players receiving a top-25 prize on either leaderboard are excluded from the draw. If fewer than 50 eligible non-ranked players qualify, each qualifying player receives 2,000 UPX; unused prize allocations will not be increased or redistributed. The participation draw does not award a badge.

### How Ties Are Settled

For the Trove Collectors leaderboard, a tie goes first to the player who collected more distinct eligible Trove types. For the Trove Bankers leaderboard, a tie goes first to the player who banked more distinct eligible Trove types during the competition. If players are still exactly tied, their order will be decided by a random draw.

### Start Exploring

The first Troves weekend begins now and ends on **Monday, October 26 at 9:00 a.m. PT**. Collect what you can, decide what belongs in your Vault forever, and see how high you can climb on both leaderboards.

Share the challenge with your friends, help each other discover new Troves, and bring your neighborhood into the competition. We cannot wait to see what you collect, what you bank, and who rises to the top. **See you in Upland!**

# UGC Submission Update: Faster Approvals Are on the Way

July 24, 2026

*​**Editor’s Note:** This post has been updated to clarify that the historical 8–12 week approval timeline reflected normal operating conditions. The current backlog extends beyond that standard, and our goal with the new system is not only to catch up, but to ultimately reduce approvals to under one week.*​

Player-created content is a huge part of Upland’s future, and we’re excited to share an important update on UGC submissions.

Our developers have finished building a brand-new** automated approval system **designed specifically for **Upland’s unique UGC pipeline**. This is a custom solution built entirely from scratch and has now **entered its testing phase**.

We’ve already processed and released our** first batch of Map Assets** using this new system and are continuing to fine-tune it as testing progresses. As our confidence in the system grows, we’ll begin moving through submissions at a **much faster pace**.

You should expect to see **additional batches **of approved Map Assets rolling out over the coming weeks. Because the system is **still being tested**, you may occasionally notice issues or inconsistencies. If you do, please let us know so we can investigate and** improve the system**.

If testing continues to go well, we expect to be fully caught up on the current submission backlog **by Harvest Season**. Once we’re caught up, our focus will shift to **further refining and optimizing** the approval process.

Under normal operating conditions, UGC approvals have** historically taken approximately 8–12 weeks**. The current backlog extends beyond that standard, but as this new system ramps up, our goal is not simply to return to the old timeline. We are working toward **reducing submission-to-approval time to under one week**.

**There’s still work ahead**, but we’re excited that this new system is already live, processing submissions, and moving us toward a much faster future for UGC creators.

# Uppie Quests Are Coming: Turn Troves Into New Friends

September 08, 2026

Troves are about to unlock much more than collecting.

After **Troves, Trove Banking, and Upland Progression** launch, the next major piece of Upland’s connected gameplay loop will arrive: **Uppie Quests**.

**Uppie Quests** will send players across the map to gather Troves, complete recipes, and earn the special **Friend Request Troves** needed to befriend new Uppies. They will also give developed properties, **Residents**, assigned Uppies, plants, and service structures **more ways to matter** together.

The loop is taking shape: **develop **properties**, collect **Troves**, choose **what to craft or bank**, complete** Uppie Quests**, **and **befriend **more Uppies who cansupport your properties and** Trove strategy.**

**Troves arrive first. Uppie Quests follow.** Here is your first look at how the systems connect.

### Find Uppie Quests Across the Map

As you explore Upland, you will be able to discover properties offering **Uppie Quests**. When an Uppie Card appears above a property, a quest is waiting there.

While property assignment began with **Level 3 and higher Uppies**, the Uppie Quest rollout is planned to open property assignment to **Uppies across all levels**.

To be eligible to spawn an **Uppie Quest, a property must have both Residents and an assigned Uppie**. Uppies of **any level** can fulfill the Uppie requirement, from Level 1 all the way up. Having both Residents and an assigned Uppie makes a property eligible to spawn quests, although an eligible property will not necessarily have a quest available at all times.

All assigned Uppies can participate in the Uppie Quest system. The difference is what else they can do on a property. For **Level 1 and Level 2 Uppies**, Uppie Quest participation will be their only property utility. Higher-level Uppies can also participate in Uppie Quests while retaining their additional abilities, such as caring for plants and, for eligible Uppies, and eventually automatically collecting Troves.

There will also be benefits for property owners when other players select an **Uppie Quest** from their property. We’ll share more about how those benefits work, along with additional details on quest availability, as we get closer to launch.

### From Trove Hunting to Uppie Questing

Every Uppie Quest is a mission built around a request from an Uppie.

Maybe an Uppie is craving breakfast and asks you to bring back a **croissant and coffee**. Gather the requested Troves, turn them in to complete the Uppie Quest, and see what you receive.

Completing an Uppie Quest gives you a **chance to receive a Friend Request Trove**, but it isn’t guaranteed. You may receive other items instead, making each completed quest a chance to earn the Friend Request Troves you’ll need to befriend new Uppies.

These special Troves are one of the key ingredients required to befriend new Uppies, and **Uppie Quests will be the primary way to earn them**.

Completing an Uppie Quest gives you a **chance to receive a Friend Request Trove**, but it isn’t guaranteed. You may receive other items instead, making each completed quest a chance to earn the Friend Request Troves you’ll need to befriend new Uppies.

These special Troves are one of the key ingredients required to befriend new Uppies, and **Uppie Quests will be the primary way to earn them**.

This is where the larger Trove system becomes even more strategic. As previously announced, Troves can serve different purposes across Upland:

- Use Troves in **crafting recipes and Uppie Quests**.
- Exchange eligible Troves for items or rewards when opportunities are available.
- Permanently bank selected Troves in your **Trove Vault** to advance Trove Banking levels and contribute to **Upland Progression**. Banked Troves cannot be withdrawn or used elsewhere, so collecting is only the beginning. **Players will decide** what to spend, what to craft with, and what to preserve permanently as part of their Upland history.

### Properties, Plants, Service Structures, and Uppies Feed the Loop

**Uppie Quests** do not sit beside Troves as a separate feature. They give the Troves you collect another purpose while strengthening the systems that help produce them.

As previously announced:

- **Healthy plants** can improve the potential for more Trove drops and rarer Troves.
- **Level 3 and higher Uppies** assigned to properties can care for plants when players keep them fed.
- **Level 5 and higher Uppies** are planned to automatically collect Troves from plants on assigned properties.
- **Level 5 and higher Uppies** can also be employed at eligible service structures, where they contribute to structure levels and can automate Trove collection.
- **Higher service-structure levels** can unlock better Trove drops from recipes.
- **Automated collection** by Uppies uses a separate daily limit from a player’s personal collection cap, allowing active play and Uppie automation to work together. That creates a **connected cycle**: develop properties and service structures, keep plants healthy, put Uppies to work, collect more useful Troves, complete more recipes and quests, and earn the **Friend Request Troves** needed to grow your Uppie collection.

### Three Quests at a Time

Players can maintain up to **three active Uppie Quests** at once.

Once all three quest slots are occupied, you will need to complete or dismiss an active quest **before accepting another**. If you discover a quest you would rather pursue, you can dismiss one to make room.

Some quests may also be time-limited, giving you a set window to gather the required Troves and complete the recipe.

**Choose carefully**. The quest you take, the Troves it requires, and the Friend Request Trove it rewards can all shape what you pursue next.

### Friend Request Troves and Befriending Uppies

Completing **Uppie Quests** rewards **Friend Request Troves**, with multiple levels available.

### Friend Request Troves and Befriending Uppies

Completing **Uppie Quests** rewards **Friend Request Troves**, with multiple levels available.

Higher-level **Friend Request Troves** can help you befriend higher-level Uppies, but earning them will require more demanding quests. Lower-level quests may use simpler recipes and more common Troves. Higher-level quests can require more complex recipes and potentially rarer Troves.

When it is time to befriend an Uppie, a befriending recipe can call for a combination of inputs, including:

- **Friend Request Troves**
- Other Troves
- UPX
- Sparklet Provide the required inputs, complete the recipe, and a newly befriended Uppie can join your collection.

That makes **Friend Request Troves** the bridge between the Troves you gather today and the Uppies you hope to meet tomorrow.

Uppies across all levels can potentially become available to befriend when the required Uppies are available in **Merge inventory**. That means befriending recipes will not always be available on demand.

Availability may change over time. Some recipes could appear during specific parts of a season, be announced in advance, remain available for longer periods, or become temporarily unavailable until inventory is replenished.

Your **Friend Request Troves** can prepare you for the opportunity. **Merge inventory** determines which friendships can be forged at that moment.

We will share more about befriending availability as the system rolls out.

### Why Build a Bigger Uppie Collection?

Uppies are becoming **active participants** in Upland’s property and Trove economy.

They can be **assigned** to properties. Eligible Uppies can **care for plants**. Higher-level Uppies are planned to **collect Troves** automatically from properties and service structures. Employed Uppies can help **level up** eligible service structures. Uppies can be traded, offer quests, and become **new friends** through the befriending system.

And there is more personality on the way. Uppies are planned to appear in **3D**, including on the map, and some may exist as truly unique one-of-one Uppies, similar to the **Dragon Mama Uppie** previously previewed.

Every new Uppie can **expand how you develop properties**, pursue Troves, complete quests, and express your place in Upland.

### Troves First. Uppie Quests Next.

Troves establish the foundation: collect across Upland, craft with what you find, permanently bank what you want to preserve, build your **Trove Vault**, and advance your **Upland Progression**.

**Uppie Quests** build on that foundation by turning Troves into missions, recipes, **Friend Request Troves**, and eventually new Uppies. Those Uppies can then return value to properties, plants, service structures, and future quests.

This is the connected Upland taking shape, with properties at the center and more of what you own, build, collect, and develop working together.

**Find the quests. Gather the Troves. Complete the recipes. Befriend the Uppies. Put them to work.**

# Uppie Quests Are Next: The Path to New Uppie Friends

November 10, 2026

​***Editor’s Note:**** We’ve clarified that the Uppie Research Lab will support befriending lower-level Uppies, while the Uppie Research Center will support higher-level Uppies. More details on the specific Uppie levels, recipes, and mechanics will be shared when Uppie Quests launch.*​

You have been exploring neighborhoods, collecting Troves, and discovering what you can craft. Next comes a new reason to head back out: **an Uppie with a request**, a quest to complete, and the** chance to befriend** a new character for your collection.

Troves 1.0 is fully launched, and **Uppie Quests are next**. Troves players gather will be useful in missions, **Friend Request Troves**, and opportunities to befriend new **Uppies**.

Starting now, the **Uppie Research Lab** and **Uppie Research Center** will become **permanently available **as public service structures. These are the **future locations for Uppie befriending recipes**, giving neighborhood builders a chance to** prepare for the next chapter** before quests and befriending arrive in a later update.

The Uppie Research Lab will be used to befriend lower-level Uppies, while the larger Uppie Research Center will be used to befriend higher-level Uppies.

How Uppie Quests Will Work

As players explore Upland, [a quest card](https://www.upland.me/events/uppie-quests-are-coming-turn-troves-into-new-friends) above an eligible property will signal that an Uppie has a request. **Properties with both Residents and an assigned Uppie **are planned to be eligible to offer quests, with **Uppies across all levels **able to participate. That gives developed properties and neighborhood activity a new reason to matter.

Accept a quest, **gather or craft** the requested Troves, and fulfill the request. One mission might feature an Uppie looking for breakfast, sending you out to find a croissant and coffee. Other requests can point toward different ingredients, recipes, and parts of the map. Players will be able to keep **up to three quests active at once**.

Completing a quest will give players a **chance to receive a Friend Request Trove**. That special Trove can become one ingredient in a befriending recipe at a Research structure. Combine the required inputs, complete the recipe, and a new Uppie can join your collection.

### Why You Will Want More Uppies

Uppies bring **personality **to a collection, but their role is becoming much more practical. Uppies of every level are planned to **take part in quests**. For Level 1 and Level 2 Uppies, quest participation is planned as their property utility. Level 3 and higher Uppies can also take part while retaining eligible roles such as **caring for plants when assigned.**

The longer-term vision goes further. In future updates, eligible Uppies are planned to **work at Service Structures**, **automatically collecting and crafting specific Troves**. That employment and **automation** will help players pursue collection, crafting, and progression goals beyond what is practical to handle manually. These systems will arrive in later updates and will not activate when the Research structures enter the store.

Collectors who want the complete lineup can grab the **Uppie Research Value Pack**, which includes The Uppie Research Lab and the Uppie Research Center for **$12**. That is **20% off regular pricing**!

The This structure will enable befriending higher level Uppies preparing builders for the moment when collected Troves can help bring new Uppies into their world. **Uppie Research Center** is a large public service structure that gives developed districts a more substantial home for future befriending recipes. *(Public Service, 37 Service Units)*

The next adventure begins when an Uppie asks for help and sends you back across Upland with a purpose. Each completed request can bring you closer to a new character for your collection and, over time, a more active role for Uppies throughout properties and Service Structures.

# We’ve Updated How We Email You

November 19, 2026

Click below to update your preferences.

We’ve changed the service that sends Upland email, and organized our messages into five subscription groups you can turn on or off. You get more control over what lands in your inbox, and the mail you want has a better chance of getting there.

Purchase receipts, security alerts, and account emails always stay on, whatever you choose. The new groups are only for the optional mail, so you can pick what fits how you play.

Here’s a look at the new groups, the two addresses to save, and how to set your preferences.

### The New Subscription Groups

You don’t have to take all of them. Choose the ones you want and leave the rest off.

- **Upland Recap.** Drops most weeks, with top strategic plays, community highlights, and a short overview of announcements you might have missed.
- **Game News & Releases.** Be the first to find out when new real-world cities launch on the map, new features go live, and gameplay guides drop. Sent around important release dates.
- **Events & Competitions.** Treasure Hunts, Troves, Racing, and more. Real-time alerts for live tournaments, global leaderboards, and in-game prize pools, sent during active challenges.
- **Just for You.** Picks based on how you play: custom milestones, deals, and strategy tips tuned to you. About once a month.
- **Style Shop.** Official apparel and gear drops, limited-edition merch, and early access to store discounts. Occasionally.

### Add These Two Addresses to Your Contacts

Upland email now comes from two addresses:

- **[[email protected]](https://www.upland.me/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection)** for news, updates, and the groups above
- **[[email protected]](https://www.upland.me/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection)** for account email like purchase receipts and password resets Please add both to your contacts or your safe senders list. Inbox filters often treat a new sending address as unfamiliar, even when the mail is from us. Saving both helps your receipts, password resets, and other account email reach your inbox instead of spam or junk.

- **Gmail.** Open [Google Contacts](https://contacts.google.com/), create a contact for each address, and save. If a message from us is in Spam, open it and choose Not spam.
- **Outlook.** Go to Settings, then Mail, then Junk email. Under Safe senders and domains, add each address and save.
- **Apple Mail and iCloud.** Add both addresses to your iCloud contacts. If a message is in Junk, move it to your Inbox.
- **Yahoo Mail.** Add both addresses to your contacts. If a message lands in Spam, select it and choose Not spam. If you use another email app, the same idea applies: save both addresses as contacts, and mark anything in junk as not junk.

# Your Block Explorers Are Ready for Their Next Adventure

October 12, 2026

***Editor’s note:** We’ve added a clarification that the images in this announcement are mockups and displayed values may change.*

​Your Block Explorers have been part of your Upland story: the characters you chose, the milestones you celebrated, and the collections you made your own. With **Troves on the way**, that collection is about to take on a new role. **Block Explorer stamina** will connect your explorers to **collecting and crafting**, giving the characters in your wallet a **bigger part to pla**y in your next adventure.

If you have a friend who has been waiting for more to do in Upland, **share this update** with them. Whether they are returning to a familiar neighborhood or discovering Upland for the first time, this is a moment to **get ready together**.

In our [earlier Block Explorer utility announcement](https://www.upland.me/events/developer-update-block-explorer-utility-structure-footprints), we introduced the direction. Now, let’s get into **how stamina will work** when Troves arrive, what you will be able to see in your wallet, and how to prepare your collection.

### Your Collection, Ready to Explore

**Stamina is the capacity your Block Explorers bring to Trove gameplay.** Collecting Troves across the map will use stamina. As you play, your available global stamina will decrease. **Receiving Trove Dust also uses stamina**, so a collection that yields dust still counts toward that activity.

Each Block Explorer contributes stamina toward your **global total**. Rarity helps determine that contribution, making the collection you hold in your wallet more meaningful in everyday play.

The Block Explorers you hold in your wallet contribute to one **global stamina total**. Your available global stamina determines how much you can collect at any given time. You do not need to switch between explorers to use it: your collection contributes to a shared pool, giving the explorers you own a **direct role in how much you can do**.

Every player starts with a baseline of **100 stamina per day**, giving everyone the ability to participate in Trove collecting. The Block Explorers you own add additional stamina capacity to your global pool, allowing you to collect more as your collection grows.

**These initial stamina values are a starting point.** We’ll be monitoring gameplay and player activity after launch and making adjustments over time to ensure the system remains balanced, rewarding, and fun for everyone.

​​*All images shown are mockups for illustrative purposes. Final stamina values and other displayed numbers are subject to change.*

### A Fresh Start Every Day

**Stamina refills every 6 hours starting at 5 PM PT ***(00:00 UTC)***.** This is a shared daily refill, rather than a separate countdown that begins whenever you use an explorer.

​​*All images shown are mockups for illustrative purposes. Final stamina values and other displayed numbers are subject to change.*

### A Fresh Start Every Day

**Stamina refills every 6 hours starting at 5 PM PT ***(00:00 UTC)***.** This is a shared daily refill, rather than a separate countdown that begins whenever you use an explorer.

Use some or all of your available stamina throughout the day, then return after the refill with your explorers replenished and ready to go again. The daily rhythm gives you a clear way to plan your collecting and crafting as you work toward your next goal.

### See What Your Explorers Can Do

You will be able to keep track of stamina without guessing:

- **Your profile and the top-left display:** check your overall Block Explorer stamina.
- **Asset Wallet → Block Explorers:** see each explorer’s maximum stamina and how much remains.
- **An individual Block Explorer’s full-screen view:** inspect its stamina alongside its asset details.

When inspecting **another player’s Block Explorer**, you will see its maximum stamina, not its current remaining stamina. That distinction matters when buying or swapping explorers: the displayed maximum tells you its capacity, not how much is available immediately.

**Transferring a Block Explorer does not refill its stamina.** If an explorer has already used all of its stamina, its new owner will need to wait for the next refill. Selling or swapping it does not create a fresh supply of stamina.

### Stamina Is the First Step. Modifiers Come Later.

We are **continuing our exploration of Block Explorer modifiers** as a future expansion of this system. Stamina establishes the foundation; modifiers are planned for a later stage and **will not be included in the initial stamina release when Troves arrive**.

Our goal is to give explorers **more individual character** in gameplay, with differences that go beyond how much stamina they bring. As shared in our initial announcement, we are exploring ideas such as **advantages **when collecting particular types of Troves, interactions with service structures, and benefits tied to** collecting a full series**.

**These are directions we are exploring, not finalized abilities or guaranteed bonuses.** Specific effects, eligible explorers, collection requirements, and timing will be shared as that work develops.

There is more we want to build here, and your feedback will help shape it. For now, the next step is **getting your Block Explorers ready **for their role in Troves.

### Grow Your Collection

**Now is the time to get your collection ready for Troves.** To help you prepare, and bring a little Halloween spirit along for the adventure, we’re introducing **Little Frights Halloween 2026**, alongside **Trove Core**, a new Terraformer celebrating the arrival of Troves in Upland. Whether you’re choosing your first collectible explorer or adding a new favorite to your wallet, these releases offer a chance to **grow your collection** ahead of stamina and the next chapter of collecting.

### Introducing Trove Core: A Terraformer for a New Chapter

**Trove Core celebrates the arrival of Troves in Upland.** With cream-colored armor, gold fittings, and a brilliant cyan energy core, this limited-edition Terraformer marks a new chapter of collecting and discovery.

With just **five mints**, Trove Core joins the ranks of Upland’s rarest Block Explorers, contributing **one of the highest stamina amounts in the game** to your collection’s global stamina pool.

And we’re thinking **even bigge**r for **Terraformers**. **Summary:** Play, Earn, Connect & Rebuild the Real World.

# Block Explorers & Traveling

our Block Explorer is your avatar on the map. Customisable. Collectible. Required.

#### What Block Explorers do

- Wander cities and discover treasures.
- Carry your identity across the map.
- Get assigned to specific cities to maximize discovery range.

#### **Block Explorer Trails**

Block explorers leave a marked trail that indicates the properties they visit as they traverse the map. This trail will start to appear after your block explorer starts moving. These trails also give you the chance to take a look at the properties your block explorer has discovered. After a certain period of time, the trail will vanish.

#### Customisation

- Visitors start with one default Block Explorer.
- Uplanders can collect more, change appearance, and assign different Block Explorers per city.
- Pro and above unlock more exclusive Block Explorers — wearable status across the map.

Getting from A to B in Upland matters. Travel is part of the strategy.

#### Two ways to travel

- **Let your Block Explorer wander.** Automatic, free, but slow and random.
- **Use a Send.** Direct your Block Explorer to a specific minted property. You can chain multiple sends to cover longer distances.

#### Travel within your city

If you own property across a city, you get free traversal between your own properties — a real competitive advantage for treasure hunting and Trove collection.

#### Travel Between Cities

Whether players are looking for a change of scenery or are chasing challenges across the map, traveling from one city to another is a big part of the Upland experience.

#### **Air Travel**

**‍**Flights are the main mode of travel between San Francisco and New York. To board a flight, send your explorer either to any plane terminal. Please note that some terminals are domestic terminals are marked with a white icon, while international terminals are marked with a yellow icon.

Each airport has several Terminals. When you head to an airport, select a Terminal in the popup window when Sending your Block Explorer to the airport. Capacity at terminals is limited every day.

Once you have reached the airport, click the terminal icon nearest to you to open the Flights Menu. This will display available flights by type and destination.

Please note that flights take time. The longer the distance, the more time it takes. Travel is not instant. This is a part of the real-world simulation Upland strives for. ‍

#### **Train Travel**

Trains function similarly to airplanes, but are slower and less expensive (like the real world). Also, there may be less routes available at a bus Terminal. For example, the bus in Arlington only travels to Dallas.

To travel on a train, first send your explorer to a train Terminal on the map. A popup window will prompt you to choose which station you wish to travel to. Select the station, then sit back and relax and enjoy the journey!

#### **Buses**

These are the slowest forms of transportation, but are often cheaper. Busses only travel to select cities. Look for the bus icon on the map to discover routes and other information before traveling.

#### **Car travel**

Players can drive personal vehicles to travel between cities on the same landmass. Car travel requires players to fuel their vehicles by staking $SPARKLET, select a destination property, and wait out a real-time travel duration based on distance.

# Choose Your Playstyle

Upland is one system with many ways to play. You don't have to pick one. Most Architects mix several. But knowing which one is calling you helps you make smart early decisions.

**District Builder.** Acquires adjacent properties, places structures, sets a theme, attracts residents. Loves seeing a neighborhood come to life.

**Marketplace Trader.** Spots undervalued properties before openings, masters collections, flips neighborhoods at the right moment, and outsmarts the competition.

**Metaventure Owner.** Opens a shop. Sells his or others' Architect's creations, vehicles, and ornaments. Earns revenue from other players.

**Event Competitor.** Races, treasure hunts, completes seasonal missions, climbs leaderboards.

**Manufacturer & Logistics.** Produces assets in factories, manages SPARKLET, runs Trade Routes.

**Collector.** Collects properties, befriends Uppies, and merges them up to Iconic Parody Uppies.

**Farmer.** Plants, harvests, raises animals. Produces Troves at scale and earns STEM through gameplay.

You can switch tracks, combine them, or invent new ones. The map remembers every choice.

## Secure your account

Account security matters because your assets have real value. Turn on Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) before you buy anything:

- Go to **Settings** in the Quick Menu.
- **SMS Authentication** sends a passcode to your phone whenever you make a transaction.
- **Google Authentication** (recommended) provides a refresh code in an authenticator app.


**To enable 2FA:**

1. Got to Settings in the Quick Menu.
2. Click "Authentication."
3. There are two types of authentication: SMS (secure), and Google Authentication (very secure)
4. SMS Authentication enables a security setting in which a passcode is sent to your mobile phone whenever you transact in Upland.
5. Google Authentication secures your account by listing a refreshing code needed whenever you want to make a transaction.
6. Scan the given QR code to add Upland as an account on Google Authenticator.
7. Enter the Upland code to verify your account.

‍Enabling 2FA protects your account from dictionary attacks, where your information on other websites may be exposed. It's highly recommended to secure your account with the best tools available to ensure the safety of your Upland assets.

title: Upland

Document: Upland

## **KYC Identity Verification**

KYC (know your customer) promotes fair play by requiring players to prove their identity. KYC is needed for various activities, including:

- Competitive Treasure Hunts (Exclusive+ Tier)
- Competitive Sparklet Treasures
- Sparklet login bonus
- Sparklet rewards
- Extracting USD to your PayPal account

KYC checks reduce the amount of Sparklet or UPX rewards doled out to bad actors. This helps level the playing field and strengthens the economy through a healthier distribution of UPX and Sparklet. ‍

Fortunately, completing a KYC check is straightforward and can be initiated in the Upland app. All players need to do is:

1. Go to the Quick Menu in the app.
2. Open the Settings menu.
3. Click on Verify Your Identity and follow the steps.


**Note:** KYC can take a few days to complete with our partner, Thunes. You will be asked to share personal information in order to verify your identity.

# Glossary

#### Some essential terms

**Architect.** A human player. You are an Architect.

**Block Explorer.** Your character on the map. Wanders autonomously. Direct it with a Send.

**Collection.** A set of related properties that, when completed, grants a UPX bonus and a permanent earnings multiplier.

**Commerce Score.** Measures a neighborhood's economic strength through Office Structures and reciprocal bonds between neighborhoods.

**FSA (Fair Start Act).** Properties reserved for newer players (net worth below 100,000 UPX). Cheaper, ideal first buys.

**Influence Score.** Measures how attractive your neighborhoods are to potential residents.

**IPU.** Iconic Parody Uppie. The rarest tier — created by merging two Level 10 Uppies.

**KYC.** Identity verification. Required for USD withdrawals and voting.

**Legit.** A collectible NFT with permanent ownership. Includes sports licenses (FIFA, NFLPA, F.C. Porto, AFA), seeds, and themed items.

**Metaventure.** A player-run shop. Sell items, earn revenue, build a brand inside Upland.

**Mint.** To become the first owner of an unminted property.

**Recipe.** A combination of Troves that, processed at a service structure, produces a higher-order good Uppies request.

**Resident Score.** Tracks how many Uppies live on your properties. Updates every 24 hours.

**Send.** A directed move that sends your Block Explorer to a specific property.

**SPARKLET.** Upland's resource/utility token. Powers building, manufacturing, fuelling vehicles, seed generation, and Metaventures. Tradable outside Upland as an ERC-20 on Ethereum and Base.

**STEM.** The dedicated Life currency. Account-bound, non-tradable. Keeps plants, farming, and animals accessible.

**Trove.** A fungible in-game item produced by structures, plants, fishing, animals, and trade routes. Used in Recipes.

**Uplander.** The status tier at which you gain permanent ownership of your assets.

**UPX.** Upland's in-game transactional currency. Fixed rate: 1,000 UPX = $1 USD. Not tradable outside Upland.

**Upland Appchain.** Upland's dedicated, transparent blockchain. Records property, structure, Uppie, and transaction data. Public block explorer at [ledger.upland.me](https://ledger.upland.me).

**Uppie.** A digital resident. Lives on properties, has personality, requests goods, levels up through merging.

# Game Tips

There's a lot going on in Upland. Here, we share tips to help new players get off to a good start. These tips are in no particular order, and there are many other guides out there to boost your experience. Feel free to check out guides from veteran players on YouTube, Telegram, Discord, Reddit, X, and other channels they broadcast to.

### Connect With The Community

The key to success in Upland is connecting with the community. Active players progress faster and enjoy a richer experience. While solo play is an option, the vibrant Upland community offers support, creativity, and fun! Join the in-game chat, [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/upland), or [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/UplandMe/) to get involved and make the most of your journey.

### Use Your Free UPX Wisely

In Upland, your first property is free! Use the UPX given to you to acquire an unowned Fair Start Act (FSA) parcel (i.e., the gray-colored FSA parcel), and you're off and running!

### Sends

Sends are the only way to move Block Explorers to a specific location (within its discovery range). Sends are needed for activities such as Treasure Hunts and city tours.

### Locate Your Block Explorer

If you take your eye off the screen, you may lose your Block Explorer! Block Explorers are always on the move without player input. If you can't find your Block Explorer, simply press the pawn icon, and you will automatically jump to your Block Explorer's location.

### Camera Controls

Feel free to move the camera from the top-down position. To do this, you can tilt the camera by holding Shift + Arrow key.

### Increase Your UPX Earnings

Properties come with a passive UPX yield that players can add to their wallets. However, the savviest players boost these property yields by completing collections. Property Collections are listed in the player's profile. We highlight some of the easier collections below.

- Newbie: Own any one property in Upland.
- City Pro: Own five properties in the same city.
- King of the Street: Own three properties on the same street.

Take a look at the Collections in each city and plan your property acquisitions for more opportunities.

### Join Activities

Some activities are really easy to join and can be rewarding. For example, players who complete a city tour (which are only available after a city first opens), earn free Sparklet *and* recuperate 100% of their registration fee.

### Location, Location, Location

When acquiring properties, look for locations that offer advantages. For example, when someone travels to your address, you earn a little free UPX. This makes properties around "hot" locations (e.g., stadiums, City Halls, Terminals, etc.) good spots to plant a flag if you can.

And if your property doesn't have anything interesting around it, build Structures, decorate with ornaments, plants, or outdoor decor, or launch a Metaventure to make it an interesting attraction! It's up to you!

# Virtual Properties

At its core, Upland is a city-builder and property trading game. Properties and their location are the foundation of the world. Buying, trading, flipping, completing collections, building neighborhoods, and discovering opportunities across the map remain central to what makes Upland unique.

title: Upland
text:
Document: Upland
Source: https://www.upland.me/events/

## Property Types

There is a property color coding that helps you to navigate faster through the map:

- **Grey:** Property owned by another player and not for sale.
- **White:** Property unminted, but out of range. Move your block explorer closer to mint it. Properties marked with an FSA marker can only be minted by Visitors and Uplanders.
- **Light green:** Property unminted and within range of your block explorer. Visitors and Uplanders can mint any light green property, while players of all other statuses cannot mint light green properties marked FSA.
- **Dark green:** Property owned by another player and listed for sale. Anyone can purchase it immediately, even if it is marked FSA.
- **Grey with blue border:** Property owned by you.
- **Dark Grey:** These are locked, unminted properties that have not yet been released.

**The Fair Start Act (FSA)** keeps Upland accessible to new players. It reserves a share of lower-priced, unminted properties for newcomers, allowing them to mint affordable land before competing with more established players. Only players below a set net-worth threshold—Visitors and Uplanders—can mint FSA-designated properties directly, though anyone can buy an FSA property that another player has listed for sale. The proportion of FSA inventory varies by city tier, from a smaller share in high-end cities to the majority in dedicated starter cities. To ensure these properties reach genuine new players, caps define how many FSA properties a single account can mint over its lifetime.

text:
Document: Upland
Source: https://www.upland.me/events/

## Property Transactions

#### Buying

- Tap any property on the map to see its listing.
- Pay with UPX (and where eligible, with USD).
- Make an offer on any property — listed or not. Your UPX sits in escrow until the owner accepts, rejects, or you withdraw the offer.

#### Selling

- Open your property → **List for Sale**.
- Set a UPX price. Where eligible, list for USD too — see "Selling for USD" in the Trade & Earn section.
- Wait, accept an offer, or relist at a new price.

#### Fees

Marketplace transactions carry a 10% community contribution fee, split 5% buyer / 5% seller. USD sales add a 5% withdrawal fee to the seller through Thunes. Fess can be subject to changes by the Upland operator.

# The Upland Constitution

*Updated June 1st, 2025 (come back here to see any updates)*

**Preamble**

We, the People of the Upland, in order to form a more perfect real-world city-builder game, establish justice, ensure domestic tranquility, provide for the common defense, promote the general welfare, protect the economy, and secure the blessings of liberty to ourselves and our posterity, do ordain and establish this Constitution for Upland.

**Declaration of Rights**

We hold these truths to be self-evident: that all Uplanders are created equal, that they are endowed with certain unalienable Rights, that among these are the ability to “Play,” “Build,” and “Trade” in Upland.

To protect the rights of all players, we submit the following constitutional “guidelines.”

**Economic Principles**

Upland has established a “real economy” sustained by players through market forces of supply and demand. Upland’s community pool partially supports these market forces by subsidizing certain economic activities of stakeholders. The collection of fees from market transactions or the earning of yield from owning a property are examples of these forces at work.

Players' attempts to exploit certain mechanics may prompt Upland operators to intervene, as described below. The following guidelines are expected to be followed by ALL players in Upland.

Players who violate these guidelines will be subject to imprisonment in Alcatraz, the prison island in the San Francisco Bay. Duration of imprisonment, fines, and sanctioning of certain activities are at the sole discretion of the Upland operating team.

---

**Article I: Asset Funneling**

Properties consistently sold to another account at an under- or over-market price may be flagged as asset funneling. This activity is damaging to the health of the Upland economy and is a severe violation. If suspected of asset funneling, players will be investigated and could face jail time and fines in Alcatraz.

**Article II: Collusion & the Expectation of “Fair” Market Pricing**

Players are expected to sell properties for realistic market valuations. Properties intentionally sold at severely under- or over-mint prices may be flagged for suspicious activity. Using property sales to move large amounts of UPX directly violates this rule.

Players are permitted to sell properties at prices above or below mint prices; however, clear abuse of this mechanism will result in jail time and possibly a fine. Suspicious use of the Property Swap mechanism could be considered collusion—or asset funneling—if said swaps are harmful to the Upland economy. Players flagged for suspicious swapping will be investigated.

**Article III: Multi Accounting**

Players can maintain **only a single account per person** in the Upland Parallel World. Those operating multiple accounts in Upland will face a jail sentence, which may be accompanied by a fine. Multi-accounting harms the Upland economy and puts other players’ assets at risk.

**Article IV: Use of In-Game Bots and Agents**

Players who employ the aid of “bots” and/or “agents” to automate in-game user activity will be subject to a jail sentence in addition to a fine. Bots used to monitor the marketplace and alert players to specific activities may not be subject to this rule, depending on how they are used.

**Article V: Due Process and Payment of Fines**

Players suspected of wrongdoing will be investigated and may be placed in Alcatraz while under investigation.

1. Players will receive an email explaining why they are under investigation.
2. Players can appeal their case by responding to the email and providing details about their circumstances.
3. After all documentation is collected, a decision will be made, and the player will be notified.

If a player is found to be in violation, they will be placed in Alcatraz until their fines are paid. (In some extreme cases, players may be required to serve a lifetime sentence in Alcatraz.) If a player is found not to have acted in bad faith, they will be notified immediately and no action will be taken.

Players who have committed wrongdoing within Upland will be expected to pay a fine in order to rectify the damage they have done to the Upland economy. This fine is intended to be a direct injection of the missing value that the player’s activity removed from the economy. Fines may also be paid in the form of burning UPX, properties, NFTs, or any other item of economic value.

To maintain the integrity of the Upland economy, we strongly advise strict adherence to these guidelines. The Upland Team will not hesitate to take action against players who violate the Upland Constitution. Please be reminded that there may be certain extreme cases in which players are jailed for violating rules not explicitly stated in the Upland Constitution.

---

#### THE BILL OF RIGHTS

**Amendment I: Trackable Token Ownership**

One of the magical things about using the blockchain, and some would say its primary benefit, is the idea of transparency. The meaning of (trackable) ownership has evolved alongside blockchain technology. At Upland, we define it as the notion that you are in primary control of your in-game assets.

When a player levels up from “Visitor” and reaches “Uplander” status (10,000+ UPX net worth), a permanent blockchain account is automatically created for the player. The private keys to that account are generated from the player’s email/password combination. Although the Upland system helps players manage their blockchain accounts, the Upland operator does not seek to control any player’s in-game assets. The account belongs to the player and allows them to manage their assets.

**Amendment II: Play**

Players in Upland can play by purchasing virtual property mapped to a real-world address. Players have the opportunity to receive special rewards by completing signature property collections, participating in daily treasure hunts, competing in live events, buying, selling, or trading digital assets, and enjoying other in-game activities.

**Amendment III: Build**

In Upland, building is the core, and players can build cities that matter. Residential and service structures, speedways for car racing, and the manufacturing of map assets allow everyone to create and customize something unique for themselves and for the community. Building in Upland requires the SPARKLET utility token.

**Amendment IV: Trade**

Upland has a player-driven economy in which supply and demand determine prices, just as in the real world. Collecting fees from visitors on properties or flipping properties is one part of Upland’s gamification, allowing players to benefit from markups.

But they can also trade other digital items in Upland, some of which they may have created themselves, making these players digital entrepreneurs and opening so-called Metaventures. Trading is facilitated by the in-app currency UPX and US$.

**Amendment V: Connect**

The Upland city-builder game is inherently social. Players will have the opportunity to connect with fellow Uplanders, learn game strategies, and collaborate with Upland’s outstanding online gaming community. Every player, without exception to Race, Creed, Gender, Sexual Orientation, Age, etc., is expected to be treated with respect, kindness, and understanding.

---

Note: The “Upland Constitution” is subject to change as the Parallel World continues to develop. Amendments will be added as necessary. The constitution serves as community guidelines for Upland’s governance. Players are always invited to review our [Terms of Service](https://upland.me/documents/Upland_Terms_of_Service_June_8_2026.pdf) and [Privacy Policy](https://upland.me/privacy-policy). Remember: Upland is a game for everyone to enjoy.

## Cars, Karts & Vans

Vehicles aren't just decorative. They can be used for racing. or sit on your properties, simulate transportation flow, and contribute to your neighborhood's connectivity and appeal.

#### Types

- **Cars.** Sedans, sports cars, classics. Some sports cars (Stock Car Pro Series, historic stock cars) support player-driven manufacturing — Architects design and sell custom versions.
- **Karts.** Built for racing. Race for UPX wagers on player-built speedways.
- **Vans & trucks.** Higher cargo capacity. More appealing to Uppies, important for future Trade Routes.
- **Semi-trucks.** Designed to move the largest amount of cargo. Used in Trade Routes.

#### Fuel

Vehicles run on SPARKLET. Larger and faster vehicles use more. SPARKLET is covered in the Trade & Earn section.

## Racing & Speedways

Racing is one of Upland's most kinetic loops. Build a speedway, host races, and wager UPX. Or race on someone else's track. Upland co-hosts with community members a seasonal racing league where winners can win big prizes, check Upland's Discord for more information.

#### What you need

- A vehicle (kart or car).
- SPARKLET for fuel.
- UPX for wagers or entry fees.

#### Speedways

Speedways are player-built tracks placed on properties. Speedway owners host races, set wagers, and earn from race fees. Monuments — Upland's rarest, most unique landmarks — host the official circuits for Upland's racing events.

#### Upland Racing

Upland also has a dedicated Racing app on [iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/upland-racing/id1668837455) and [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.upland.racing) with its own race events and partnerships (including Stock Car Pro Series).

## Boats & Marinas

Boats extend Upland from land into water. Lakes, bays, and oceans become active zones for exploration and resource collection.

### The four vessel classes

- **Skiff.** Lakes and nearshore waters. Entry-level.
- **Speed Boat.** Same waters, faster.
- **Pilot House.** Farther offshore. Unlocks deeper waters.
- **Fishing Yacht.** Rare. Deep ocean access. The biggest fish Troves.

### Marinas

Marinas are a dedicated property type. They trade like any other property, but only houseboats. The marina where you dock determines the waters you can access — the marina location is a strategic asset on its own.

## Treasure Hunting

Treasure hunting is the adventure mechanic. Send your Block Explorer across a city to find hidden treasures within a time limit. Proximity hints guide you. Speed matters.

#### Three tiers

- **Standard.** Available to all players.
- **Limited.** For Uplander status and above.
- **Exclusive.** Higher ranks. Includes pinata mini-games and bigger rewards.

#### Treasure Rush

Treasure Rush is a timed event in which players spawn and collect as many treasures as possible within a 30-minute window. No sends are consumed during a Rush. Leaderboards rank the top hunters per city.

#### Strategy

- Own property across the city you're hunting in — free traversal to your own properties is a real advantage.
- Higher-tier cities offer more substantial rewards.
- Watch for "Sparked Up" Treasure Tiers during SPARKLET Weeks — treasure chests can drop SPARKLET.

# Troves & Recipes

Troves are the game layer that brings Upland together. At their core, Troves connect gameplay to location. Exploring the map, interacting with assets, caring for plants, visiting neighborhoods, using structures, and participating in activities can all become ways to earn Troves and progress through the world. Instead of each system standing on its own, Troves create a shared layer where player actions, location, and decisions begin to connect.

Troves are designed around a simple but powerful idea: almost anything in Upland can become an output, and almost any output can become an input somewhere else. Properties, structures, map assets, vehicles, plants, neighborhoods, service structures, and activities can all output Troves, and your Block Explorers are how you go out and collect them. Players can then bring those Troves to specific locations like service structures, input them into recipes, and unlock rewards such as rare Troves, Uppies, SPARKLET, UPX, STEM, yield and more.

For example, a player might send their Block Explorer to plants and Service Structures across Upland to discover what each one holds. In the future, other systems like fishing, farming, trade routes, racing, treasure hunting and more will also connect into Troves, giving players different ways to gain rewards based on how they choose to play.

Those Troves can then be used in recipes at service structures. A bakery might turn wheat and milk into bread. A workshop might turn resource Troves into crafted goods. A kitchen, shop, or other service structure might require different combinations of Troves to produce new outputs, rare Troves, SPARKLET, STEM, UPX, or other rewards.

This is where the systems start to reinforce each other. A player may own a property, build on it, decorate it, plant on it, and help make the surrounding neighborhood more active. Those assets can output Troves. Those Troves can then become inputs at service structures, where recipes turn them into new rewards and progression opportunities.

#### How collecting works

Collection is location-based. Move your Block Explorer close to a Service Structure or plant, then press and hold it to attempt a collection. A normal tap only opens its details. What you find goes into your Trove Wallet, which you open from the Troves icon on the map. Different structures and plants hold different possibilities, and collecting from ones you own improves your chances of finding rarer Troves.

Every collection attempt uses Block Explorer stamina. Every player gets a free baseline, and every Block Explorer in your wallet adds to one shared pool that refills on a regular timer, with no need to equip or switch explorers. Rarer explorers with smaller editions contribute more stamina.

Every collection attempt uses Block Explorer stamina. Every player gets a free baseline, and every Block Explorer in your wallet adds to one shared pool that refills on a regular timer, with no need to equip or switch explorers. Rarer explorers with smaller editions contribute more stamina.

Each object has its own cooldown for each player. Your cooldown doesn't block other players, and it doesn't affect other objects of the same type. Collecting from an object that's still on cooldown for you can give Trove Dust instead of a regular find, so moving on to fresh locations is the better use of stamina.

#### Recipes

Recipes are discovered through collecting. The first time you find a Trove, you'll see the recipes that use it as an ingredient. When you hold everything a recipe needs, go to the Service Structure where it's available and fulfill it right there. Crafting uses up the ingredients and always gives you the recipe's stated result, sometimes with bonus rewards on top. Some crafted Troves are ingredients in deeper recipes, so you can work your way from everyday finds up to much bigger collection goals.

Uppies are one important path within this larger system. As players explore Upland, they may encounter Uppies across the map who request specific Troves that can only be obtained through certain recipe outputs. To fulfill those requests, players will need to gather the right Troves, bring them to the right service structures, and run the recipes that produce what the Uppie is looking for.

Fulfilling those requests can help players to befriend Uppies. Once befriended, Uppies can be employed at service structures to help level those structures up. Higher-level service structures can unlock better recipes, create more useful outputs, and make that location more powerful within the broader Troves loop.

## Watch The Announcement Video

#### Example recipe

Wheat Trove + Milk Trove → at a Bakery service structure → Bread Trove. An Uppie nearby has requested Bread. Deliver it to complete the quest and earn a Friend Request Trove. Use it to befriend the Uppie, and you can mint that Uppie at Level 1.

#### Recap: The loop

- Collect Troves through gameplay (your structures, your plants, your fishing trips, farming, and more).
- Combine Troves through Recipes at service structures.
- Discover and complete Uppie Quests — missions tied to properties with Uppie Cards, requesting specific Trove combinations.
- Earn Friend Request Troves as a quest reward, then use them (plus other Troves, UPX, and Sparklet) to befriend a new Uppie.
- Eventually, merge two same-level Uppies to level up. Repeat. ​Players can hold up to three active Uppie Quests at a time — complete or dismiss one to take on another.

#### Banking & Progression

Not every Trove needs to be spent. **Trove Banking** lets you permanently deposit Troves into your **Trove Vault** instead of using them in a recipe or quest — banked Troves can't be withdrawn or used again, but they're the foundation of your long-term Upland history. Each Trove has its own banking tiers (Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, and beyond), and you don't need to unlock them in order — collect enough of a Trove and you can jump straight to a higher tier. The quantity needed for each tier varies by Trove, and you bank from your Trove Wallet once you hold enough copies. Because banking is permanent, it's worth thinking about which Troves you'd rather keep for recipes.

Banking feeds directly into the **Upland Progression System** — a numerical level shown on your profile, along with your next milestone and its reward. Banking Troves is the main way to advance it, and other objectives such as developing properties can count toward it, too. Progression runs alongside your existing Upland status (Uplander, Pro, Executive, Director, and above) rather than replacing it, and each milestone comes with its own rewards — Map Assets, UPX, collectibles, and more.

#### Strategy

- The more developed your neighborhood, the more Trove variety you can produce.
- Multiple service structures in one city mean you can complete more Recipes without long sends.
- Specialists who produce one Trove type at scale can trade with neighbors who produce a different type.
- Collecting from structures and plants you own improves your odds of rarer Troves.
- Spread your stamina across fresh locations rather than revisiting objects that are on cooldown.

#### Five categories

- **Care.** Items that maintain plants, animals, and other living elements.
- **Resource.** Raw materials. STEM-bearing plants produce these.
- **Social.** Items tied to community interaction (petting, visits, gatherings).
- **Utility.** Tools and components that feed into other Recipes.
- **Valuables.** Higher-rarity items are sometimes tradable.

#### Where Troves come from

# What is Upland?

Upland is the only persistent, real-world city-builder and property trading game on a shared map that never resets. You acquire, trade, and develop virtual properties tied to actual addresses across 50+ cities, attract digital residents called Uppies, and trade in an open economy powered by three purpose-built currencies. Upland launched in 2019.

## At a glance

- **Real-world map.** 50+ cities tied to actual streets.
- **No resets.** You own it. What you build stays until you sell or redevelop.
- **Player-driven economy.** Over $20M in player-to-player trades.
- **Free to play.** Mobile and web. Only email and password required to begin.
- **Real stakes.** Eligible digital assets can be sold for USD and withdrawn to PayPal after identity verification. Availability, fees, and tax obligations vary by region.

## How it feels to play

Upland blends the satisfaction of city-building with the energy of a live, player-driven economy. Travel takes time, supply chains matter, and collaboration wins. You acquire properties at real addresses, develop them with structures, and watch the world respond — residents move in, neighborhoods come alive, and the things you build start producing goods that fuel everything else. Factories turn resources into items that move across the map and sell through player storefronts. Plants and farms need time to grow and care to thrive.

Go solo or coordinate with neighbors to deliver bigger projects faster. There are many ways to play — trade, build, explore, create, compete, collaborate — and you're in charge of deciding.

# Why Upland Is Different

Most city-builder games give you a private map only, which resets (all the time). Upland gives you the real world, one shared map, and a memory.

**One shared map, real places.** Every Architect (you, the player) acts on the same global map tied to real-world addresses. Your property becomes your block. Together with other Architects, you shape your neighborhood.

**A real player-driven economy.** Players own and trade properties, structures, vehicles, plants, animals, and Uppies peer-to-peer. Supply, demand, and strategy set every price — not an algorithm.

**Permanence.** Live since 2019. No seasonal wipes. The first San Francisco properties from 2019 still belong to the players who minted and haven't sold them.

**Sell in-game items.** Eligible digital assets can be listed on Upland's marketplace for USD via Thunes, our regulated payment partner. After identity verification, you can withdraw USD proceeds to PayPal. Live since 2020. Regional availability, fees, and tax obligations apply.

**Accessible depth.** Start fast on mobile or web. Go deeper by completing collections, property trading, shops, city planning, finding troves, befriending Uppies, and live events.

**A positive, helpful community.** Many years of accumulated assets, social bonds, player-run businesses, and shared history. AI can't clone this.
